content.intro: In this lesson, you will explore xml feeds and syndication within XML in Web Services and Data Integration. You will connect its syllabus topics to an inspectable example, check the expected result, and note tool/version limits.
content.why_it_matters: XML Feeds and Syndication matters because XML workflows rely on explicit structure and predictable processing. The lesson helps you reason about rss fundamentals, avoid a common misunderstanding, and make a result reproducible for another developer.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: XML-based integrations use explicit message structure and often a published service contract. Correct interoperability depends on matching namespaces, schema/version assumptions, character encoding, transport behavior, and error conventions.

content_blocks.title: Connect the subtopics
content_blocks.text: This lesson explicitly covers: RSS fundamentals; Atom feeds; Feed structure; Metadata and timestamps; Parsing feed data safely. Treat these as connected parts of one workflow: define the structure, make the relevant assumptions explicit, and verify a result with a small known input.

content_blocks.run_instructions: Inspect this example as text. Run it only in a processor that supports the shown language/version; the standard CodeLeaf playground previews HTML/CSS/JavaScript only and does not execute XML, XSD, XPath, XSLT, XQuery, Python, or SQL. Check the exact protocol/version specified by the service. SOAP 1.1 and SOAP 1.2 use different envelope namespace identifiers, and WSDL/service-binding support varies between client libraries.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the sample to its exact starting state before each experiment. Change one element, attribute, expression, or constraint at a time, then compare the result with the expected behavior.

content_blocks.title: Version and safety checkpoint
content_blocks.text: Distinguish well-formedness, schema validity, and application-level correctness; they are different checks.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Create a small synthetic example that demonstrates “RSS fundamentals”. Then add one boundary case involving “Atom feeds”. Write down what should happen before testing, and record the exact output or processor message afterward.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming a document is correct because it looks readable.
common_mistakes.why: Visual appearance does not prove well-formedness, schema validity, correct namespace handling, or application-level meaning.
common_mistakes.fix: Parse and validate the document with the intended processor, then assert its meaning using a focused test.

common_mistakes.problem: Mixing specification features with processor support.
common_mistakes.why: A standard may define features that a specific runtime does not implement.
common_mistakes.fix: Record the version and feature support; test with the actual target processor.

common_mistakes.why: Missing values, wrong types, namespace differences, or boundary inputs can expose failures.
common_mistakes.fix: Add a valid case, an invalid case, and an edge case to the verification notes.
